info.title: [PREVIEW] Revolut Wallet Partner Callbacks
info.description:
:::warning[Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

Endpoints you host and Revolut calls. Implement them to this contract so we can pull data
on demand. Revolut is always the client; you are the server.

- **Fetch transaction outcomes**: `POST /transaction-outcomes/search`. Called after a customer pays
  with a Revolut card, we ask what `passes` and `digital_receipts` that transaction produced.
- **Fetch a pass update**: `GET /passes/{partner_reference}`. We poll for the current state of
  a pass so we can refresh it in the customer's wallet.

Passes are identified by **your own** `partner_reference`, which is the value you set when you return a
pass here, and that Revolut echoes back when it calls the companion Revolut-hosted API
(`/docs/api/revolut-wallet-partner`).

The base URL in `servers` is illustrative; you register your real base URL during onboarding.

:::info
Start with the [Revolut Wallet guide](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/guides/revolut-wallet/introduction) and [Get started](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/guides/revolut-wallet/get-started) to onboard your business.
:::

post.summary: [PREVIEW] Fetch transaction outcomes for a transaction
post.description:
:::warning[Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

Revolut calls this after detecting a Revolut-card transaction at your business. Match the
transaction from the `transaction_context` and return what it produced.

Revolut only calls for eligible purchase transactions, so `transaction_context.total` is
always non-negative. Refunds and cancellations are never sent as new lookups - they
surface as `410` (void outcome) on retries.

Despite using `POST`, this is a **safe lookup** with no side effects: `POST` is used only to
carry the match criteria in the body (keeping `rrn` out of URLs/logs and allowing the key to
grow). No `Idempotency-Key` is required.

**Status semantics (these drive our retry behaviour):**
- `200`: transaction matched; return the outcomes (the `passes` and `digital_receipts` arrays may be empty).
- `202`: transaction not ready yet (settlement lag); we retry, honouring `Retry-After`.
- `404`: transaction definitively not found; we stop retrying.
- `410`: transaction existed but its outcome is void (refund/cancellation); we stop.
- `429` / `503`: temporary capacity issue; we retry, honouring `Retry-After`.

:::note
Validate Revolut's credentials (mTLS, JWS, or OAuth 2.0) and reject any unauthenticated request with `401`.
:::

:::info
See [Auto-provision transaction outcomes](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/guides/revolut-wallet/operations/transaction-outcomes) for matching logic and examples.
:::

200.description: Transaction matched. Returns the outcomes it produced.

boarding_pass.summary: A single boarding pass produced by the transaction

generic_pass.summary: A generic pass with a positional presentation

value.default: Entry is subject to the event terms and conditions.

generic_pass_semantic_fallback.summary: A generic pass using semantic fallback

generic_pass_header.summary: A generic pass with a header row

digital_receipt.summary: A tax-inclusive digital receipt with a tip produced by the transaction

split_tender_receipt.summary: A GBP 25.00 receipt for a purchase where GBP 12.20 was charged to the Revolut card

none.summary: Transaction matched, but produced no outcomes

202.description:
Transaction accepted but its outcome is not ready yet (settlement lag). Revolut retries,
honouring `Retry-After`.

:::note
Return no body with `202`.
:::

404.description: Transaction definitively not found. Revolut will stop retrying.

value.message: No transaction found for this rrn and merchant_id.

410.description: Transaction outcome is void (refund/cancellation). Revolut will stop retrying.

value.message: The transaction outcome is void due to a refund or cancellation.

get.description:
:::warning[Pre-release preview]
This is a pre-release preview of upcoming documentation.
The features, workflows, and UI described here are subject to change before the final release.
:::

Return the latest state of the pass identified by `partner_reference` (the reference you
assigned). Revolut calls this on a schedule and on demand to refresh what the customer sees.

**Support conditional requests.** You generate and return an `ETag` header with every `200`
response. It is an opaque token representing the current state of the pass. Revolut stores
it and sends it back as `If-None-Match` on subsequent calls. If the pass is unchanged since
that `ETag`, reply `304 Not Modified` (no body). If it has changed, return `200` with the
full pass and a fresh `ETag`.

**Status semantics:**
- `200`: pass returned.
- `304`: unchanged since the supplied `ETag`.
- `404` / `410`: pass gone. Revolut stops polling it.

:::note
Validate Revolut's credentials (mTLS, JWS, or OAuth 2.0) and reject any unauthenticated request with `401`.
:::

:::info
See [Update a pass](https://developer.revolut.com/docs/guides/revolut-wallet/operations/update-pass) for the push-vs-poll model and polling cadence.
:::

parameters.name: partner_reference
parameters.description:
Your own reference for the pass, as set when you created it (Partner API `POST /passes`)
or returned in a transaction-outcomes response. Send the **bare value** here — do not use
the `ref:` prefix (that form is only for the Partner API `PUT /passes/{id}`).

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description:
An `ETag` previously returned by your `200` response to this endpoint. Revolut sends it
back so you can skip re-sending an unchanged pass. Return `304 Not Modified` if the
pass state is the same as when you issued this `ETag`.

200.description: Current pass state. Excludes `template_id` (immutable, set at creation).

boarding_pass.summary: A boarding pass with updated gate

generic_pass.summary: A generic pass with a positional presentation

404.description: Pass not found. Revolut stops polling it.

value.message: No pass found for this partner_reference.

410.description: Pass permanently gone. Revolut stops polling it.

value.message: The pass has been voided or refunded.

mtls.description:
**Mutual TLS.** Revolut presents a client certificate signed by the Revolut Partner CA.
Validate it against the Revolut CA chain from onboarding and reject any request without a
valid Revolut certificate. Your Partner ID is bound to it. Can be used on its own, or
layered on top of JWS for defence in depth.

jws.name: Jws-Signature
jws.description:
**Message signing (JWS).** Revolut signs the request body together with a timestamp (to
prevent replay) as a detached JWS (`RS256`/`ES256`) using the Revolut Partner signing key
whose certificate you registered during onboarding, and sends the compact JWS in the
`Jws-Signature` header. You verify it against the registered Revolut certificate. May be
used on its own or together with mTLS.

oauth2.description:
OAuth 2.0 **client credentials**. Revolut requests a short-lived access token from your
token endpoint (authenticating with its onboarding credential: `client_secret`,
`private_key_jwt`, or its mTLS certificate) and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
The token carries the `passes.read` scope. May be used on its own or together with mTLS.

scopes.passes.read: Read transaction outcomes and pass state.

ApiVersion.name: Revolut-Api-Version
ApiVersion.description:
Contract version Revolut is calling with. This contract defines `2026-07-01`.

:::note
If you receive a version you do not implement, respond with `400`.
:::

RequestId.name: Request-Id
RequestId.description: Revolut's correlation id for this request. Echo it back in your response.
Correlation id for the response. Echo the incoming `Request-Id` when present.

ETag.description:
Opaque strong entity tag for the current pass state. Do not use the `W/` weak validator
prefix. Return a fresh value with every `200` response.

RetryAfter.description:
Integer seconds Revolut should wait before retrying (not the HTTP-date form).
`0` means retry immediately.

TransactionOutcomesSearchRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /transaction-outcomes/search`. Contains the transaction context
Revolut sends for you to match.

TransactionContext.description:
Identifiers Revolut supplies so you can match the originating transaction.
The acquiring institution ID (DE 32 in ISO 8583) is collected during onboarding and used
by Revolut to match transactions to you, but is not sent in the transaction context.

rrn.description: ISO 8583 Retrieval Reference Number of the original payment.

merchant_id.description: Card acceptor identifier (DE 42 in ISO 8583 messaging); identifies the sub-merchant for aggregators.

transaction_at.description: Timestamp of the purchase, UTC, ISO 8601.

total.description:
Amount charged to the Revolut card, supplied for stronger matching. When returning
digital receipts, Revolut does not compare this amount or currency with the values in
those receipts. You remain responsible for returning the correct receipt data.

TransactionOutcomes.description:
What a Revolut-card transaction produced. Currently the passes and digital receipts tied
to the transaction. Revolut ignores unknown fields in this response, so you may add
fields without breaking compatibility.

Digital receipt amounts and currencies are merchant-supplied. Revolut does not validate
their decimal scale, rounding, arithmetic relationships, or consistency with
`transaction_context.total`, another receipt, or another field in the same receipt. You
are responsible for returning accurate, internally consistent receipt data. Revolut does
not reject or retry a response because its receipt amounts or currencies do not reconcile.

A response that fails schema validation is treated as invalid: Revolut ingests none of
the outcomes from it and retries the request using its internal backoff policy, stopping
when that policy is exhausted. The number and duration of retries are not part of this
contract, and Revolut does not send an error notification when it drops a response.

split_tender.description:
Whether the digital receipts in this response cover a purchase paid using the Revolut
card and at least one other payment method. Applies to the complete response, not to an
individual receipt. This field provides payment context only; Revolut does not use it
to validate amounts or currencies. If omitted, defaults to `false`.

passes.description: Passes the transaction produced; may be empty.

digital_receipts.description: Digital receipts the transaction produced; may be omitted or empty. Revolut accepts their monetary and currency values as supplied; you are responsible for their accuracy and consistency.

error_id.description: Your trace id, if you have one.

Money.description: ISO 4217 monetary amount, represented as strings to preserve decimal precision. Amounts are non-negative.

amount.description: Non-negative decimal amount as a string (e.g. "72.40").

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. GBP, EUR, USD).

Image.description: An image used by pass branding.

asset_ref.description: Reference to an image asset managed by Revolut.

ColourScheme.description: Explicit colours used to render a branded pass.

Branding.description: Optional visual branding for a pass.

brand_name.description: Brand name displayed on the pass.

logo.description: Logo image used by the pass.

background_image.description: Background or hero image used by the pass.

predefined_style.description: Predefined visual style for the pass.

colours.description: Explicit colour scheme for the pass.

Issuer.description: Issuer information displayed on a pass.

issuer_full_name.description: Full legal name of the issuer.

default.description: Fallback text when no localisation matches.

localisation_key.description: Key resolved against Revolut's localisation catalogue at render time.

Action.description: A button rendered on the pass (e.g. "Open website", "Get directions").

id.description: Unique identifier for the action within this pass.

type.description: Documented values: `open_external_url`. External URL domain needs to be registered at onboarding.

label.description: Display label for the button, with optional localisation.

importance.description: Relative prominence of this action (5 = primary, 1 = least prominent).

Presentation.description: How a trigger is presented to the customer.

title.description: Title text for the notification or tile, with optional localisation.

description.description: Body text for the notification or tile, with optional localisation.

Trigger.description: A context-aware notification that nudges the customer (e.g. proximity alert, time before event).

id.description: Unique identifier for the trigger within this pass.

importance.description: Relative prominence of this trigger (5 = high, 1 = low).

time_offset.description: ISO 8601 duration before the target (e.g. `PT1H` for 1 hour before departure).

radius_meters.description: Radius in meters around the `location_targets` coordinates for the proximity alert.

field_target.description: Name of the semantic field to watch for changes (e.g. `boarding.gate`).

presentation.description: How the trigger is presented to the customer (notification, tile).

PassBase.description: Fields common to every pass type.

partner_reference.description: Your own reference for the pass; use it to match the pass in your system.

type.description:
Pass type discriminator. Selects the `semantics` structure for boarding, event, and loyalty
passes. Generic passes are rendered from their `fields` and `presentation`. Documented values:
`boarding_pass`, `event_pass`, `loyalty_pass`, `generic_pass`.

version.description: Your monotonically increasing version; bump on every change.

relevant_at.description: When the pass becomes time-relevant (departure, event start); drives polling cadence.

branding.description: Optional visual branding for the pass.

issuer.description: Optional issuer information displayed on the pass.

triggers.description: Context-aware notifications that nudge the customer.

Passenger.description: Passenger details for a boarding pass.

full_name.description: Full name of the passenger as it appears on the boarding pass.

fare_class.description: Human-readable fare class (e.g. Economy, Business, First).

fare_class_code.description: IATA fare class code (single letter, e.g. Y for Economy, J for Business).

frequent_flyer_program.description: Name of the frequent flyer program the passenger belongs to.

frequent_flyer_number.description: Membership number within the frequent flyer program.

name.description: Full name of the airport (e.g. London Luton Airport).

city.description: City where the airport is located.

Flight.description: Flight details for a boarding pass.

flight_number.description: Flight number without the carrier code (e.g. 2241, not SJ2241).

carrier_code.description: IATA or ICAO carrier code (2 alphanumeric characters).

carrier_name.description: Display name of the operating carrier.

operating_carrier_code.description: Carrier code of the actual operating carrier (for codeshare flights, this may differ from `carrier_code`).

aircraft_type.description: IATA aircraft type code (e.g. A320, B738).

Boarding.description: Boarding details for a flight — gate, seat, and boarding time.

gate.description: Boarding gate at the departure airport.

boarding_group.description: Boarding group or zone (airline-specific, e.g. A, B, 1, 2).

sequence_number.description: Boarding sequence number assigned to the passenger.

seat_class.description: Seat class label (e.g. Economy, Premium Economy, Business).

Booking.description: Booking details for a boarding pass.

pnr.description: Passenger Name Record — the booking reference from the airline's reservation system.

booking_reference.description: Alternative booking reference (e.g. agency or GDS reference), if different from the PNR.

Validity.description: Validity window for a pass — when it becomes active and when it expires.

valid_from.description: Start of the pass validity period, UTC, ISO 8601.

valid_until.description: End of the pass validity period, UTC, ISO 8601.

BoardingPassSemantics.description: Semantic tags for a boarding pass.

validity.description: Optional validity window for the pass.

BoardingPassCreate.description: A boarding pass being created, comprising the pass content plus its render template.

template_id.description:
Identifier of a pre-registered branding/layout template to render this pass with.
If omitted, Revolut uses the default template for your partner account, which may
not match your brand. Including it ensures your pass is rendered with the correct
visual design. Set at creation and immutable; not accepted when updating a pass.

Event.description: Event details for an event pass.

edition.description: Edition or iteration of a recurring event (e.g. 2026, Season 5).

held_on.description: Calendar day of the event (use `starts_at` for the precise start time).

starts_at.description: Start time of the event, UTC, ISO 8601.

ends_at.description: End time of the event, UTC, ISO 8601.

doors_open_at.description: Time the venue doors open, UTC, ISO 8601.

city.description: City where the venue is located.

section.description: Section or block within the venue (e.g. Block 112, Section C).

Ticket.description: Ticket details for an event pass.

booking_reference.description: Booking or order reference for the ticket purchase.

Participant.description: Participant details for an event pass (e.g. conference attendee).

company.description: Company or organisation the participant represents.

role.description: Role or title at the event (e.g. Speaker, Attendee, Volunteer).

name.description: Name of the organising company or individual.

EventPassSemantics.description: Semantic tags for an event pass.

validity.description: Optional validity window for the pass.

EventPassCreate.description: An event pass being created, comprising the pass content plus its render template.

template_id.description:
Identifier of a pre-registered branding/layout template to render this pass with.
If omitted, Revolut uses the default template for your partner account, which may
not match your brand. Including it ensures your pass is rendered with the correct
visual design. Set at creation and immutable; not accepted when updating a pass.

Member.description: Member details for a loyalty pass.

full_name.description: Full name of the loyalty program member.

member_id.description: Membership number or ID within the loyalty program.

member_since_on.description: Date the member joined the programme.

TierProgress.description: Progress towards the next loyalty tier.

current.description: Current progress value as a string (e.g. points earned this period).

target.description: Target value required to reach the next tier, as a string.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the progress values (e.g. points, stays, flights).

PointsBalance.description: Points balance for a loyalty pass.

value.description:
Current points balance as a non-negative decimal string with up to six fractional digits.
Do not use a sign, exponent notation, or redundant leading zeros. Compare values as decimals,
so `"1500"` and `"1500.00"` are equivalent.

unit.description: Unit label for the balance (e.g. points, miles).

monetary_value.description: Optional monetary equivalent of the points balance.

NextReward.description: Next reward the member can unlock with their points.

description.description: Human-readable description of the reward (e.g. "Free coffee voucher").

points_required.description: Points required to unlock the reward, as a string.

Loyalty.description: Loyalty program details for a pass.

program_name.description: Display name of the loyalty program.

tier.description: Current tier level of the member (e.g. Gold, Silver, Bronze).

next_reward.description: Next reward the member can unlock.

LoyaltyPassSemantics.description: Semantic tags for a loyalty pass.

loyalty.description: Loyalty program details (tier, balance, next reward).

validity.description: Optional validity window for the pass.

LoyaltyPassCreate.description: A loyalty pass being created, comprising the pass content plus its render template.

template_id.description:
Identifier of a pre-registered branding/layout template to render this pass with.
If omitted, Revolut uses the default template for your partner account, which may
not match your brand. Including it ensures your pass is rendered with the correct
visual design. Set at creation and immutable; not accepted when updating a pass.

FieldId.description: Unique identifier for a custom field within a generic pass.

DataCategory.description:
Data category for the field. The category describes the type of information carried by
the field.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `identity` | Primary subjects, holder names, pass titles, or card names. |
| `status` | State metrics, membership tiers, or operational updates such as Delayed, Gold Tier, or Active. |
| `time` | Temporal coordinates such as Start Time 19:00, boarding times, or expiry times. |
| `location` | Spatial coordinates or places such as Seat 14C, Gate A7, venues, or addresses. |
| `verification` | Human-readable fallback codes, member IDs, or order references. |
| `attribute` | Domain properties such as Meal: Vegan, Class: Business, or Points: 1,400. |
| `governance` | Contractual, legal, or reference information such as terms, disclaimers, or support phone numbers. |

FieldSemanticType.description:
Optional semantic tag associated with the field. 

The following values are currently exposed by the typed pass schemas in current API version.
Use the public snake_case path names.

**Boarding passes**

`passenger.full_name`, `passenger.fare_class`, `passenger.fare_class_code`,
`passenger.frequent_flyer_program`, `passenger.frequent_flyer_number`, `flight.flight_number`,
`flight.carrier_code`, `flight.carrier_name`, `flight.operating_carrier_code`,
`flight.departure_airport.iata`, `flight.departure_airport.name`, `flight.departure_airport.city`,
`flight.departure_airport.country_code`, `flight.departure_airport.terminal`,
`flight.arrival_airport.iata`, `flight.arrival_airport.name`, `flight.arrival_airport.city`,
`flight.arrival_airport.country_code`, `flight.arrival_airport.terminal`,
`flight.scheduled_departure_at`, `flight.scheduled_arrival_at`, `flight.aircraft_type`,
`boarding.gate`, `boarding.boarding_at`, `boarding.boarding_group`, `boarding.sequence_number`,
`boarding.seat`, `boarding.seat_class`, `booking.pnr`, `booking.ticket_number`,
`booking.booking_reference`, `validity.valid_from`, `validity.valid_until`.

**Event passes**

`event.name`, `event.category`, `event.edition`, `event.held_on`, `event.starts_at`,
`event.ends_at`, `event.doors_open_at`, `venue.name`, `venue.address`, `venue.city`,
`venue.country_code`, `venue.coordinates.lat`, `venue.coordinates.lng`, `venue.gate`,
`venue.section`, `venue.row`, `venue.seat`, `ticket.number`, `ticket.booking_reference`,
`ticket.type`, `participant.full_name`, `participant.company`, `participant.role`,
`organiser.name`, `validity.valid_from`, `validity.valid_until`.

**Loyalty passes**

`member.full_name`, `member.member_id`, `member.member_since_on`, `loyalty.program_name`,
`loyalty.tier`, `loyalty.tier_progress.current`, `loyalty.tier_progress.target`,
`loyalty.tier_progress.unit`, `loyalty.points_balance.value`, `loyalty.points_balance.unit`,
`loyalty.points_balance.monetary_value.amount`, `loyalty.points_balance.monetary_value.currency`,
`loyalty.next_reward.description`, `loyalty.next_reward.points_required`,
`validity.valid_from`, `validity.valid_until`.

FieldData.description:
Shared content, semantic metadata, and optional formatting hints for a generic-pass custom field.
The field `id` is referenced from the pass `presentation` configuration. When neither the pass
nor its template provides a presentation, every field must provide `data_category` and
`semantic_type`; `importance` remains optional.

label.description: Display label for the field, with optional localisation.

value.description: Display value for the field, with optional localisation.

data_category.description:
Category describing the information carried by the field. Required on every field when
rendering falls back to semantic metadata; otherwise optional.

semantic_type.description:
Semantic identifier associated with the field. Required on every field when rendering falls
back to semantic metadata; otherwise optional.

importance.description:
Optional relative prominence of the field (5 = highest, 1 = lowest), used for semantic
rendering.

text_alignment.description: Preferred text alignment when the renderer supports it.

date_style.description: Preferred date display style for a `date_time` value.

time_style.description: Preferred time display style for a `date_time` value.

is_relative.description: Whether a date and time value should be presented relative to the current time.

ignores_time_zone.description: Whether a date and time value should be shown without time-zone conversion.

number_style.description: Preferred display style for a numeric value.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code used when presenting a currency value.

RowItem.description: A field placed in a positional presentation row.

field_id.description: ID of the primary field displayed in this slot.

join_field_id.description: Optional ID of a field joined to the primary field in the same slot.

alignment.description: Horizontal placement of the slot within its row.

PresentationRow.description: A row in a positional generic-pass presentation.

PositionalPresentation.description:
Maps field IDs into header, primary, secondary, and footer sections. This layout may be supplied on the
pass or by its template. Every referenced ID must match a field in the pass, and every field ID
must appear at least once as a `field_id` or `join_field_id` when this layout is used.

header.description: Optional header section row, displayed before the primary section.

primary.description: Primary section row, displayed after the header when provided.

secondary.description: Optional secondary section rows, in display order.

PresentationConfig.description:
Optional explicit positional layout for a generic pass. When omitted, the template presentation
is used. When neither provides a presentation, the pass is rendered from semantic metadata on
every field.

GenericPass.description:
A fields-driven generic pass. The `fields` array defines reusable field data and an optional
`presentation` selects a positional layout. When `presentation` is omitted, the template
presentation is used. When neither provides a presentation, the pass is rendered from semantic
metadata: every field must provide `data_category` and `semantic_type`; `importance` is optional.

fields.description: Custom fields available to the selected presentation layout.

presentation.description:
Optional explicit layout. When omitted, the template presentation is used. When neither
provides a presentation, rendering falls back to semantic metadata on every field.

GenericPassCreate.description: A generic pass being created, comprising the pass content plus its render template.

template_id.description:
Identifier of a pre-registered branding/layout template to render this pass with.
If omitted, Revolut uses the default template for your partner account. Set at creation
and immutable; not accepted when updating a pass.

PassCreate.description:
A pass as created/provisioned, i.e. a concrete pass type plus the `template_id` that renders it.
Used when a pass is created (`POST /passes`) or provisioned from a transaction outcome. New pass types
may be added over time and are available in all supported API versions.

ReceiptAddress.description: Postal address printed on a digital receipt.

ReceiptMerchant.description: Merchant information displayed on a digital receipt.

name.description: Merchant display name, e.g. as shown at the till or storefront.

legal_name.description: Full legal name of the merchant, e.g. for VAT purposes.

merchant_id.description: Card acceptor identifier (DE 42 in ISO 8583); echoes the `merchant_id` from the transaction context.

vat_number.description: Merchant VAT registration number, where applicable.

coordinates.description: Geographic coordinates of the merchant location.

website_url.description: Merchant HTTPS website. Its hostname and every redirect destination hostname must be registered during partner onboarding. If any hostname is not registered, Revolut ignores only `website_url` and continues processing the receipt.

ReceiptAmount.description:
A merchant-supplied non-negative decimal amount in the receipt's `currency`. Beyond checking
that the value is a decimal string, Revolut does not validate or normalise its scale, rounding,
leading zeros, or relationship to other monetary fields. You are responsible for returning
accurate and internally consistent amounts that follow the currency and accounting rules that
apply to the purchase.

ReceiptLineItem.description:
A single itemised line on a digital receipt. Per-line `tax_amount` and `discount_amount` are
scalar aggregates; the named breakdown lives on the receipt-level `taxes` and `discounts`
arrays. Every receipt discount must be allocated across the line `discount_amount`s when
`line_items` are present.

description.description: Item description as printed on the receipt.

quantity.description: Quantity as a decimal string; supports fractional quantities such as "42.5" litres of fuel.

unit_of_measure.description: Unit of measure for the quantity, e.g. `unit`, `kg`, `litre`, `metre`, `hour`.

unit_price.description: Price per unit of measure, as a decimal string; includes tax when the receipt's `tax_included` is true. May use additional fractional precision for fuel, weighted goods, and similar purchases. You are responsible for its scale and its relationship to the line total.

discount_amount.description: Total discount applied to this line, as a decimal string. Omission is treated as zero when reconciling receipt discounts.

tax_amount.description: Total tax charged on this line, as a decimal string.

total_amount.description:
Authoritative discount-adjusted line total, as a decimal string. When `quantity` and
`unit_price` are present, this equals `quantity` x `unit_price` minus `discount_amount`;
it includes tax when the receipt's `tax_included` is true. You are responsible for this
calculation; Revolut does not recalculate the value.

sku.description: Your SKU or product identifier for the item.

notes.description: Free-text modifiers or options, e.g. "Oat milk".

product_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of the product page. Its hostname and every redirect destination hostname must be registered during partner onboarding. If any hostname is not registered, Revolut ignores only `product_url` and continues processing the receipt.

image_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of a product image. Its hostname and every redirect destination hostname, including CDN hostnames, must be registered during partner onboarding. If any hostname is not registered, Revolut ignores only `image_url` and continues processing the receipt.

ReceiptTax.description: A named tax summary line on a digital receipt, e.g. "VAT (20%)".

rate.description: Tax rate as a decimal-string percentage, e.g. "20.00" for 20%.

amount.description: Tax amount contributing to `tax_total` when that aggregate is supplied, as a decimal string.

description.description: Display label for the tax line.

ReceiptDiscount.description: A named discount summary line already reflected in the receipt totals, e.g. "Loyalty member discount".

description.description: Display label for the discount line.

amount.description: Discount amount already reflected in line totals and `subtotal`, as a decimal string.

DigitalReceipt.description:
A digital receipt for a purchase made with a Revolut card, as returned in a transaction outcomes response. Purchase receipts only.
All amounts are non-negative decimal strings in a single currency. Receipts are rendered
natively by Revolut; no template is required. `total` is the authoritative final amount after
discounts, including any tax and tip.

Amount semantics:
- All amounts are decimal strings in the receipt's `currency`.
- You are responsible for the accuracy, decimal scale, rounding, currency consistency, and
  arithmetic relationships of every amount. Revolut accepts the monetary and currency values as
  supplied and does not recalculate them or compare them with the originating transaction,
  another receipt, or another field in this receipt.
- Aggregate fields other than `total` are optional. An omitted aggregate is not supplied and
  must not be interpreted as zero. The relationships below apply when every referenced field
  is present.
- Line `unit_price` is before discount. Line `total_amount` is after discount, and every
  receipt discount is already reflected in the line `discount_amount`s when `line_items` are
  present.
- `tax_included: true`: line `unit_price` and `total_amount` include tax; `total` equals the
  sum of line `total_amount`s plus `tip_total`; `subtotal` equals the sum of line
  `total_amount`s minus `tax_total`, equivalently `total` minus `tax_total` minus `tip_total`.
- `tax_included: false`: line prices exclude tax; `subtotal` equals the sum of
  line `total_amount`s; `total` equals `subtotal` plus `tax_total` plus `tip_total`.
- `discounts` and `discount_total` only summarise discounts already reflected in line totals
  and `subtotal`; never subtract them again. When the corresponding values are present,
  `discount_total` equals both the sum of `discounts[].amount` and the sum of line
  `discount_amount`s, treating an omitted line `discount_amount` as zero.

`partner_receipt_reference` is your unique reference for the receipt. It identifies the
receipt across your partner account, not just within one response: reusing it for a different
receipt, including in a later response for another transaction, is a contract violation.
Receipts are immutable once returned; Revolut deduplicates them by `partner_receipt_reference`
across retries, and references must be distinct within a single response. When a known
reference arrives with different content, Revolut keeps the first receipt it accepted and
ignores the differing one. Revolut ignores unknown fields in this response, so additional
fields may be added without breaking compatibility.

partner_receipt_reference.description: Your own unique reference for the receipt; use it to match the receipt in your system. Identifies the receipt across your partner account; must be distinct within a single response.

receipt_number.description: Human-readable receipt or order number as printed on the merchant receipt.

issued_at.description: Date and time the merchant issued the receipt, in RFC 3339 format with `Z` or a numeric UTC offset. Preserve the merchant-local offset when available.

merchant.description: Merchant the purchase was made at.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code that you assign to all amounts on the receipt. You are responsible for ensuring it is correct; Revolut does not compare it with the originating transaction or other receipts in the response.

tax_included.description:
Whether `line_items[].unit_price` and `line_items[].total_amount` include their
corresponding tax. `total` always includes all tax charged. See the schema description
for the `subtotal`/`tax_total`/`total` relationship in each case.

line_items.description: Itemised purchase lines whose `total_amount`s are discount-adjusted. Omit when you cannot itemise the receipt.

taxes.description: Named tax breakdown summarised at the bottom of the receipt. When `tax_total` is also present, it equals the sum of these amounts.

discounts.description: Named discount breakdown already reflected in line totals and `subtotal`. When `discount_total` is also present, it equals the sum of these amounts.

subtotal.description: Optional discount-adjusted amount before tax and tip. Omission means the value was not supplied; see `tax_included` for the exact semantics.

tax_total.description: Optional total tax charged on the purchase. Omission means the value was not supplied; when `taxes` is present, this equals the sum of its amounts.

discount_total.description: Optional summary of discounts already reflected in line totals and `subtotal`; never subtract it again. Omission means the value was not supplied. When present, it equals the `discounts` total and, when `line_items` is present, the sum of line `discount_amount`s.

tip_total.description: Optional total tip included in `total`. Omission means the value was not supplied and must not be interpreted as zero.

total.description: Merchant-supplied final purchase amount after discounts, including tax and tip. Revolut treats this value as authoritative and does not recalculate it.

receipt_url.description: HTTPS URL of the full receipt hosted by you, e.g. an HTML or PDF version. Its hostname and every redirect destination hostname must be registered during partner onboarding. If any hostname is not registered, Revolut ignores only `receipt_url` and continues processing the receipt.

PassUpdate.description:
The updatable state of a pass, i.e. one of the concrete types selected by `type`. Used both when you
push an update and when Revolut polls you for the latest state. Excludes `template_id`, which is
fixed at creation. New pass types may be added over time and are available in all supported API versions.

BadRequest.description:
Malformed request: an unsupported `Revolut-Api-Version`, an invalid path parameter,
or an invalid request body.

Unauthorized.description:
Missing or invalid Revolut credentials: no or failed mTLS certificate, an invalid
JWS signature, or a missing/invalid OAuth 2.0 access token.

Forbidden.description:
Authenticated, but the credential lacks the required scope/permission (e.g. an OAuth token
without `passes.read`).

value.message: The credential does not have the passes.read scope.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded. Revolut retries, honouring `Retry-After`.

value.message: Rate limit exceeded. Retry after the specified delay.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Temporary capacity issue. Revolut retries, honouring `Retry-After`.
